workspace.label: Workspaces
workspace.createDescription: Create a new workspace to organise your tools.
workspace.editDescription: Change the workspace name or description.
workspace.nameTaken: A workspace with that name already exists.
workspace.resetDescription: This will delete every stored piece of data, including all workspaces and their contents. This action cannot be undone.

home.betaDescription: This application is at a very early stage of development. Bugs, breaking changes or data loss can happen at any time. Do not store critical information without an external backup.
home.privacyDescription: Everything is stored locally in your browser. Nothing is sent to any external server.
home.evolvingDescription: New tools and utilities will be added regularly to cover more investment needs.
home.workspacesDescription: Each workspace works as an independent database inside the app. You can create several to separate portfolios, strategies or simulations, and switch between them at any time.
home.toolsDescription: Access the available utilities to analyse and manage your investments. New tools will be added over time.

portfolioRebalancing.title: Portfolio Rebalancing
portfolioRebalancing.description: Works out the transfers needed to rebalance your fund portfolio towards the target allocation you define.

sp500.intro: Simulate your DCA investment using historical S&P 500 data to see the best, worst and current case. This tool runs on S&P 500 historical data since 1927. Values are in US dollars (USD). It does not matter if you work in another currency — this tool is only an estimate.

financialFreedom.intro: Work out how many years you need to keep contributing to live off S&P 500 returns alone, taking your future expenses into account. Based on historical data since 1927.
financialFreedom.noExpenses: No expenses configured. Add expenses to calculate your financial freedom.

portfolioRebalancing.intro: Enter your current portfolio and your target allocation to work out the optimal transfers.

current.title: Current Portfolio
current.description: Funds you currently hold. The percentage is calculated automatically.
current.empty: There are no funds in the current portfolio.

target.title: Target Portfolio
target.description: Desired allocation after rebalancing. The amount is calculated automatically.
target.empty: There are no funds in the target portfolio.
target.mustSum100: Percentages must add up to exactly 100%.
target.copyToast: Target portfolio copied to the clipboard

calculate.splitHint: Transfers will be split into {parts} equal parts for DCA.
calculate.singleHint: A single transfer per movement will be calculated.

transfers.title: Required transfers
transfers.balanced: Your portfolio is already balanced. No transfers are needed.
transfers.single: {count} transfer is needed to rebalance your portfolio. | {count} transfers are needed to rebalance your portfolio.
transfers.split: {count} transfer is needed, split into {parts} parts (DCA). | {count} transfers are needed, split into {parts} parts (DCA).

mortgage.intro: The APR published by the bank does not account for what tied products really cost you: it only includes the mandatory ones, at list price. Here three APRs are calculated —the official one, the real one with what you are actually going to sign, and the one you would get without optional tied products— and each product is charged only with the extra cost versus buying it on your own.

empty.title: No offers yet
empty.description: Add the mortgages you are considering, with their conditions, costs and tied products. You can also load two examples with plausible Spanish market figures —one fixed and one variable— to see how the tool works. They are not real offers nor a recommendation.

tabs.deleteDescription: Its conditions, tied products and early repayments will be removed. This cannot be undone.

globalSettings.title: Global data for the comparison
globalSettings.description: Principal, term, property price, savings, opportunity cost and Euribor scenario. They are shared by every offer so the comparison stays fair.
globalSettings.hint: This is where the data shared by every mortgage is set —{summary}—.

common.euriborTooltip: Seed for the three predefined scenarios. No market value is stored in the tool so it does not age silently.
common.opportunityCostToggle: Simulate the opportunity cost of the capital not paid up front
common.expectedReturnHint: The expected return is a hypothesis, not a promise. Set it to 0% to switch off its effect without disabling the simulation.

scenario.hint: The scenario is shared by the whole comparison so it stays fair. Points are interpolated linearly and the value stays constant after the last one. The ±1 pp shift over 5 years is a sensitivity convention, not a forecast.

conditions.tinFixedTranche: Nominal rate of the fixed tranche (%)

costs.lcciNote: Since Spanish Law 5/2019 (LCCI) the bank pays notary, agency, registry and stamp duty; the client pays the appraisal and the deed copy. All of them can be set in case the offer is old, a subrogation or a special case. Only the items charged to the client feed into the APR.
costs.openingFeeHint: On the principal, always charged to you.
costs.earlyRepaymentNote: Tiers preloaded with the LCCI caps for each loan type. They are editable: an offer predating the law or a foreign one may fall outside them, and in that case you only get a warning.

bindings.note: The chargeable cost is always the difference: what it costs at the bank minus what you would spend on that product if the mortgage did not exist. It can come out negative if the bank product is cheaper than yours.
bindings.empty: No tied products. Add the ones the bank requires or offers you to see their real cost.

nomina.label: Salary direct deposit
nomina.hint: The most profitable one: zero cost. It usually requires a minimum monthly income and, with two borrowers, both salaries.

recibosDomiciliados.label: Direct debits
recibosDomiciliados.hint: Electricity, water, gas or phone. Zero cost; sometimes a minimum number of bills is required.

tarjetaCredito.label: Credit card
tarjetaCredito.hint: Typical annual fee of €30–50, often free the first year. If it requires a minimum spend you would make anyway, the outside cost is 0.

cuentaMantenimiento.label: Account with maintenance fee
cuentaMantenimiento.hint: Maintenance fee charged if the account requirements stop being met.

seguroHogar.label: Home insurance
seguroHogar.hint: Building cover is required by law with a mortgage, so the outside cost is almost never 0.

seguroVida.label: Life / repayment insurance
seguroVida.hint: Not required by law even if the bank presents it as such. Common variant: a financed single premium.

seguroProteccionPagos.label: Payment protection insurance
seguroProteccionPagos.hint: Almost nobody would buy it elsewhere, so the whole cost is charged. Cover comes with many exclusions.

seguroSalud.label: Health insurance
seguroSalud.hint: Outside cost 0 if you would not want it; equal to your current policy if you already have one.

seguroCoche.label: Car insurance
seguroCoche.hint: Often net negative: if the bank's is cheaper than yours, you save.

alarma.label: Alarm / security
alarma.hint: Monthly fee of €30–45, above market. Outside cost 0 unless you already have an alarm.

planPensiones.label: Pension plan
planPensiones.hint: The contribution is not an expense, it is your own saving. The real cost is the fees versus your alternative, plus the illiquidity.

inversionFondos.label: Investment funds / managed portfolio
inversionFondos.hint: Typical bank fee of 1.2–1.9% versus 0.2–0.4% for an index tracker. It usually comes with a minimum holding period.

cuentaValores.label: Securities account / bank broker
cuentaValores.hint: Custody and trading fees versus your current broker.

otro.label: Other
otro.hint: Free-form, for whatever each bank comes up with.

bindingForm.title: Tied product
bindingForm.description: The cost charged to the mortgage is always the difference between what it costs at the bank and what you would spend on that product if the mortgage did not exist. It can be negative.
bindingForm.required: Mandatory to be granted the loan
bindingForm.annualMarketHint: What you would spend on this if the mortgage did not exist. 0 if you would never buy it.
bindingForm.annualDiscount: Bank discount in the first year (%)
bindingForm.coverYearsHint: If it covers fewer years than the term, automatic renewal at the same amount is assumed.
bindingForm.investmentNote: The contribution is not an expense: it is your own saving. The chargeable cost is the fees and the worse management versus what you would buy on your own.
bindingForm.requirementHint: Informational: it does not enter the calculation, but it flags the risk of losing the discount.

investment.title: Cost assistant — {name}
investment.description: The money is not lost, but it is managed more expensively than if you invested it yourself. Two portfolios are simulated in parallel with the same contributions and the chargeable cost is how far apart they drift.
investment.bankGap: Extra return lost to worse management (%)
investment.inheritedHint: {value} inherited from the global data. It is the same gross return for both portfolios: what changes is the fees, not the market.
investment.taxDeductionHint: Pension plans only, at your marginal rate. Careful: what you deduct now is taxed on withdrawal.
investment.wouldInvestAnyway: I was going to invest that money anyway
investment.notInvestingHint: As this is not money you were going to invest, the contributions also count as a cash outflow and their recovery as an inflow once the holding period ends, so the APR captures the cost of having it locked up.
investment.verdictPending: Add the tied product to the comparison to see the verdict.
investment.verdict: Buying the bank product costs you {cost} over {years} years; the {bonus} discount saves you {savings} →
investment.contributed: Total contributed: {value}. The chargeable cost is the gap between the two portfolios, not the contribution.

prepayments.note: One-off or recurring payments. “Reduce term” keeps the instalment and shortens the loan; “reduce instalment” keeps the term and recalculates the instalment. The applicable fee comes from the tiers set in Costs and fees.
prepayments.summary: Total interest saved: {savings}; fees paid: {fees}. The loan is cancelled in month {month} of {termMonths}.

opportunity.disabled: Opportunity cost is switched off. Enable it in the global data to simulate what happens to the savings you do not put into the down payment.
opportunity.intro: Borrowing less saves interest but locks up savings. This is the other half of the picture: the money this offer leaves free, invested at {returnPct} for {years} years and taxed at {taxPct} on withdrawal. The return and the tax are edited in the global data.
opportunity.negativeDownPayment: The principal of this offer exceeds the property price, so there is no down payment to make. Check the principal or the price.
opportunity.notAffordable: Your savings do not cover the down payment plus the costs: you are {value} short. The offer drops out of the ranking, but it is still calculated.

summary.official: Official APR {official} · without optional tied products {without}

amortization.title: Amortisation schedule — {name}
amortization.description: Month by month with the rate applied after discounts, the net cost of the tied products charged to each month and the early repayments.

comparisonPanel.singleOffer: Only one offer is loaded: here you see its results on their own. Add another one for the comparison to make sense.
comparisonPanel.disabledCount: {count} mortgage disabled and out of the comparison. Re-enable it from its tab menu. | {count} mortgages disabled and out of the comparison. Re-enable them from their tab menu.

comparisonTable.title: Comparison
comparisonTable.description: The winner is decided by real APR: it includes the costs charged to you, the arrangement fee and the net cost of the tied products. Net worth sits alongside as a second reading, but it depends on a hypothetical return and does not drive the ranking.
comparisonTable.empty: There are no active mortgages in the comparison.

hints.upfront: Charged to you, arrangement fee included
hints.bindingGross: What you pay the bank for the products
hints.bindingNet: Net of what you would spend elsewhere anyway
hints.officialApr: Bank of Spain criterion: mandatory tied products only, at gross cost
hints.realApr: The metric that decides the ranking

comparisonTable.rankingMismatch: The two rankings disagree: the offer with the lowest real APR is not the one that leaves you with the most net worth. That usually happens when the cheap one demands a bigger down payment and leaves you with less invested savings. The lowest real APR is still highlighted, because net worth depends on a return that has not happened yet.
comparisonTable.crossover: The cumulative cost of the two best offers crosses in year {year}: before that point the other one comes out ahead.
comparisonTable.sortHint: Click a header to sort. Non-viable mortgages (savings do not cover the down payment plus costs) are shown, but stay out of the ranking.

worthIt.title: Are the tied products worth it?
worthIt.description: For each product the mortgage is recalculated with and without it. It is worth it if the interest you save thanks to the discount beats its cumulative net cost. The break-even point is the maximum net cost at which it would stop being worth it.
worthIt.empty: No active mortgage has tied products.
worthIt.inactiveNote: Disabled: figures for what would happen if you signed it.

charts.installmentDescription: Monthly instalment at the end of each year. On variable rates you can see the effect of every review.
charts.cumulativeCostDescription: Upfront costs + interest + net cost of tied products + fees, accumulated. Where two lines cross, the better option changes.
charts.outstandingDescription: What is left to repay to the bank at the end of each year.
charts.netWorthDescription: Portfolio of the free capital net of tax minus the cumulative cost of the mortgage.
charts.empty: Enable a mortgage to see the charts.

sensitivity.title: Euribor sensitivity
sensitivity.description: Real APR of each offer in each index scenario. A fixed rate barely moves; on a variable one the range is the measure of the risk you take on.
sensitivity.note: In green, the winning offer within each scenario. If it changes from one column to another, the decision depends on where the Euribor goes and not only on the offer.

warnings.feeCapExceeded: Some early repayment fee exceeds the LCCI cap ({cap}%) for this loan type. It is calculated anyway, in case the offer predates the law.
warnings.invalidPrincipalOrTerm: Invalid principal or term: check the global data or this mortgage's own data.
warnings.floorAboveCap: The floor is above the cap: check the rate limits.
warnings.negativeDownPayment: The principal granted exceeds the property price: the down payment comes out negative.
warnings.notAffordable: Your available savings do not cover the down payment plus the costs of this offer.
warnings.requiredBindingInactive: “{name}” is mandatory and disabled: the bank would not grant the mortgage without it.
warnings.singlePremiumRenewal: “{name}”: the premium covers {coverYears} of the {years} years; renewal at the same price is assumed.
warnings.bonusCapped: The accumulated discount exceeds the {cap} pp cap and has been trimmed.
